watering.title: 💧 Watering
watering.summary: Keep the soil evenly moist, but never constantly waterlogged.
guidance: 🌱 Check the top 2–3 cm of soil before watering. Water when it begins to feel slightly dry.
☀️ Hibiscus usually needs more frequent watering during hot, sunny weather.
🪴 Container-grown hibiscus may dry out faster than plants growing in the ground.
🌧️ Reduce watering during rainy or cool periods when the soil stays moist longer.
🚫 Do not keep the roots continuously submerged in water.
watering.frequency: Usually 2–4 times per week depending on heat, rainfall, pot size and soil drainage.
watering.warning: ⚠️ Overwatering can cause yellow leaves, poor root health and fungal problems. Underwatering may cause wilting and bud drop.

sunlight.title: ☀️ Sunlight
sunlight.summary: Hibiscus grows and flowers best with plenty of bright sunlight.
guidance: 🌞 Aim for around 6 hours of sunlight or strong bright light.
🌸 Morning sunlight is generally beneficial.
🔥 In extremely hot weather, some protection from harsh afternoon heat can help prevent stress.
🏡 Keep potted plants in a bright location with good air circulation.
sunlight.warning: ⚠️ Too little sunlight may reduce flowering and cause weak, stretched growth.

temperature.title: 🌡️ Temperature
guidance: 🌿 Protect the plant from extreme cold.
🔥 Provide sufficient water during very hot conditions.
🌬️ Good airflow helps reduce stress and disease-friendly humidity.
temperature.warning: ⚠️ Sudden environmental changes can cause stress, leaf drop or bud drop.

soil.title: 🪴 Soil
soil.summary: Use fertile soil that holds some moisture but drains excess water well.
recommended_mix: 🏖️ Coarse material such as sand or perlite for improved drainage
soil.warning: ⚠️ Avoid heavy soil that remains saturated for long periods.

fertilizer.title: 🌱 Recommended Fertilizer
fertilizer.recommended: 🌱 19-19-19 NPK water-soluble fertilizer for general growth. 🌸 00-52-34 (MKP) can be used as a phosphorus-rich fertilizer during flowering.
guidance: 🌱 Use 19-19-19 NPK during active vegetative growth for balanced nutrition.
🌸 During flowering, 00-52-34 (MKP) can be used as a phosphorus-rich fertilizer when appropriate.
🧴 Follow the exact dosage and application instructions printed on the fertilizer product label.
💧 Avoid applying concentrated fertilizer to very dry soil unless the product label specifically allows it.
🚫 Do not repeatedly apply high doses in an attempt to produce more flowers.
fertilizer.schedule: Generally every 2–4 weeks during active growth, depending on the fertilizer product and label instructions.
fertilizer.warning: 🚨 Over-fertilizing can damage roots, burn leaves and cause nutrient or salt buildup in containers.

pruning.title: ✂️ Pruning
guidance: ✂️ Remove dead, damaged or clearly diseased branches.
🌿 Light pruning can encourage bushier growth.
🧹 Use clean tools to reduce the risk of spreading disease.
🚫 Do not heavily prune a severely stressed plant unless necessary.
pruning.warning: ⚠️ Disinfect pruning tools when moving between diseased and healthy plants.

calendar.watering: Check soil moisture every day; water when the upper soil layer begins to dry.
calendar.leaf_inspection: Inspect leaves every 7 days for spots, pests, whiteflies, mealybugs, rust or powdery growth.
calendar.fertilizer: Review feeding every 2–4 weeks during active growth, following the fertilizer label.
calendar.pruning: Remove dead or damaged growth during regular weekly inspection.

safety_care: 🧤 Wear gloves when handling fertilizers, pesticides or unknown plant treatments.
🧴 Never exceed the product label rate.
🌬️ Apply sprays only in suitable conditions and avoid strong wind.
🐝 Protect pollinators by avoiding unnecessary pesticide use on open flowers.
👶 Keep fertilizers and chemicals away from children and pets.
important_warning: 🚨 Do not treat every yellow leaf as a disease; watering, nutrient problems and environmental stress can produce similar symptoms.
🚨 Do not combine multiple pesticides or fungicides unless the product labels specifically permit it.
🚨 If the plant is rapidly declining, inspect roots, watering conditions and pest activity in addition to leaf symptoms.

watering.title: 💧 Watering
watering.summary: Keep moisture reasonably consistent without waterlogging the root zone.
guidance: 🌱 Water when the upper layer of soil begins to dry.
☀️ Increase attention during hot and dry weather.
🌧️ Reduce watering when rainfall keeps the soil wet.
💧 Deep, appropriate watering is generally better than keeping the soil constantly saturated.
watering.frequency: Often 2–3 times per week, but actual needs depend on weather, soil and container size.
watering.warning: ⚠️ Irregular watering can stress chilli plants and may affect flowering and fruit development.

sunlight.title: ☀️ Sunlight
sunlight.summary: Chilli generally performs best in bright sunlight.
guidance: 🌞 Aim for approximately 6–8 hours of direct sunlight where conditions are suitable.
🏡 Ensure the plant receives good light for healthy growth and fruit production.
🌬️ Avoid extremely enclosed locations with poor airflow.
sunlight.warning: ⚠️ Low light can lead to weak growth and reduced flowering or fruit production.

temperature.title: 🌡️ Temperature
guidance: 🌱 Protect plants from prolonged cold conditions.
🔥 During intense heat, monitor for wilting and water stress.
🌸 Extreme temperatures may affect flowering and fruit set.
temperature.warning: ⚠️ Very high heat combined with poor watering can cause severe stress.

soil.title: 🪴 Soil
soil.summary: Use fertile, loose and well-draining soil.
soil.warning: ⚠️ Poor drainage increases the risk of root problems and disease development.

fertilizer.title: 🌱 Recommended Fertilizer
fertilizer.recommended: 🌱 19-19-19 NPK water-soluble fertilizer during general vegetative growth. 🌶️ 13-00-45 (Potassium Nitrate) can be used as a potassium-rich fertilizer during flowering and fruit development.
guidance: 🌱 Use 19-19-19 NPK during active vegetative growth for balanced nutrition.
🌸 During flowering and fruit development, 13-00-45 (Potassium Nitrate) provides nitrogen and a higher proportion of potassium.
🌶️ Balanced nutrition is important for healthy flowering and fruit development.
🧴 Follow the exact dosage and application instructions on the fertilizer label.
🚫 Avoid excessive nitrogen, which can encourage excessive leafy growth.
fertilizer.schedule: Review feeding every 2–4 weeks during active growth according to the fertilizer product label.
fertilizer.warning: 🚨 Excess fertilizer can burn roots, damage leaves and cause nutrient imbalance.

pruning.title: ✂️ Pruning
guidance: ✂️ Remove clearly dead or severely diseased leaves.
🌿 Avoid excessive pruning of a healthy fruiting plant.
🧹 Keep pruning tools clean.
pruning.warning: ⚠️ Remove and dispose of heavily diseased material appropriately instead of leaving it near healthy plants.

calendar.watering: Check soil moisture daily during hot weather.
calendar.leaf_inspection: Inspect every 7 days for thrips, mites, spots, curling and nutrient deficiency symptoms.
calendar.fertilizer: Review feeding every 2–4 weeks during active growth according to the product label.
calendar.pruning: Remove dead or severely affected material during inspection.

safety_care: 🧤 Wear protective equipment when applying crop-protection products.
🌬️ Do not spray during strong wind.
🧴 Follow the exact product label and required waiting period before harvest.
🚫 Do not randomly mix pesticides or fertilizers.
important_warning: 🚨 Leaf curling can have several causes, including pests, viruses, heat stress or nutrient problems.
🚨 Yellow leaves do not automatically mean fertilizer is required.
🚨 Check the underside of leaves for mites, thrips and other small pests.

watering.title: 💧 Watering
watering.summary: Provide consistent moisture while avoiding waterlogged soil.
guidance: 🌱 Check the soil before watering.
💧 Water near the root zone rather than frequently wetting the leaves.
☀️ Increase monitoring during hot weather.
🌧️ Avoid unnecessary watering after sufficient rainfall.
🪴 Use pots with drainage holes for container-grown tomatoes.
watering.frequency: Often every 1–3 days in hot conditions, but the correct schedule depends on weather, soil and plant size.
watering.warning: ⚠️ Very inconsistent watering can contribute to plant stress and some fruit-quality problems.

sunlight.title: ☀️ Sunlight
sunlight.summary: Tomatoes generally need strong sunlight for vigorous growth and fruit production.
guidance: 🌞 Aim for around 6–8 hours of direct sunlight when possible.
🌿 Ensure good airflow around plants.
🏡 Avoid overcrowding container plants.
sunlight.warning: ⚠️ Poor sunlight can reduce healthy growth and fruit production.

temperature.title: 🌡️ Temperature
guidance: 🌸 Very high temperatures can reduce successful flowering and fruit set.
🌱 Protect plants from prolonged cold.
💧 Monitor watering more carefully during hot periods.
temperature.warning: ⚠️ Extreme heat can cause stress and wilting even when the plant has no disease.

soil.title: 🪴 Soil
soil.summary: Use fertile, well-draining soil rich in organic matter.
soil.warning: ⚠️ Avoid reusing heavily diseased soil or leaving infected plant debris around the growing area.

fertilizer.title: 🌱 Recommended Fertilizer
fertilizer.recommended: 🌱 19-19-19 NPK water-soluble fertilizer during general growth. 🍅 13-00-45 (Potassium Nitrate) can be used as a potassium-rich fertilizer during flowering and fruit development.
guidance: 🌱 Use 19-19-19 NPK during early vegetative growth for balanced nutrition.
🌸 During flowering and fruit development, 13-00-45 (Potassium Nitrate) provides a higher proportion of potassium.
🍅 Avoid excessive nitrogen during fruiting because it can encourage excessive leafy growth.
🧴 Follow fertilizer product label rates and application instructions.
🚫 Do not increase fertilizer dosage to try to obtain faster growth or larger fruits.
fertilizer.schedule: Review feeding every 2–4 weeks during active growth depending on the fertilizer product and label instructions.
fertilizer.warning: 🚨 Over-fertilization can damage roots and cause nutrient imbalance or salt buildup.

pruning.title: ✂️ Pruning and Plant Support
guidance: ✂️ Remove dead or heavily diseased leaves where appropriate.
🌿 Keep lower foliage from resting on wet soil when possible.
🪢 Support plants using stakes or cages.
🧹 Keep tools clean when working with multiple plants.
pruning.warning: ⚠️ Do not remove large amounts of healthy foliage at once.

calendar.watering: Check soil moisture daily, especially during hot weather.
calendar.leaf_inspection: Inspect every 7 days for early blight, late blight, leaf mold, spots, pests and leaf curling.
calendar.fertilizer: Review feeding every 2–4 weeks during active growth according to the fertilizer label.
calendar.pruning: Check and remove dead or severely affected leaves during weekly inspection.

safety_care: 🧤 Use protective equipment when handling fertilizers or plant-protection products.
🍅 Follow the required pre-harvest interval for agricultural chemicals.
🐝 Avoid unnecessary chemical treatment when pollinators are active.
important_warning: 🚨 Tomato leaf spots can have multiple causes; do not assume every spot is the same disease.
🚨 Late blight and early blight require careful differentiation because management decisions can differ.
🚨 Avoid wetting leaves unnecessarily when fungal disease pressure is high.
🚨 If symptoms spread rapidly, isolate the affected plant area and inspect nearby plants.
